page: Microsoft Azure F4als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor built on x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU features 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced vector instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of total memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage on this instance, necessitating the attachment of network-based storage volumes for persistent data. Additionally, the instance includes no GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core computing capabilities, with stress-ng single-core execution reaching 3783.49, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. High single-threaded throughput is also reflected in compression workloads, recording 40.46 GB/sec in gzip compression and 18.11 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance aligns with the middle tier, delivering a multi-core stress-ng score of 15088.73 and a PassMark CPU score of 13471.73. Memory throughput measures 53.17 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 34.25 GB/sec for write operations.

While the instance delivers high performance for small language model text generation (333.29 tokens/sec on a 135M model), prompt processing on larger models like the 7B parameter architecture registers in the bottom 25 percent at 30.07 tokens/sec due to limited RAM capacity and CPU thread count. Given its high-frequency cores and lean memory footprint, the F4als_v7 delivers cost-efficient performance for compute-bound tasks, code compilation, microservices, batch processing, and compression utilities.
description: Microsoft Azure F4als_v7 is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 4-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using x86_64 architecture, clocking up to 4.5 GHz with dedicated CPU allocation. The instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction support. The server includes no bundled local storage and no GPU hardware, relying on external network storage for persistent filesystem needs. Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core compute performance, with top-decile results in single-core stress-ng tests and single-threaded gzip compression. Multi-core metrics, memory bandwidth, and web serving throughput fall within the average range. Due to its lean memory capacity and lack of local NVMe storage, the configuration is cost-effective for pure CPU-intensive workloads rather than data-heavy tasks. It is best suited for batch processing, web serving frontends, compression tasks, and software build pipelines.
